memos.headline: Relative strength favors AMZN, GOOGL, JPM, and XOM while AAPL flashes oversold and PG remains in a structural downtrend
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AMZN (+9.2% 1w, RSI 69, only -2.6% from highs) and GOOGL (at its 52-week high, +85.9% over 26w, +29.1% 12w relative strength vs SPY) are the strongest momentum names, though both are approaching overbought territory. AAPL's RSI of 27.2 and -4.9% gap below its 50-day mean suggest a short-term oversold bounce is possible, but the -7.9% 4-week relative strength vs SPY is concerning and I need to see it reclaim ~272 (the 50-day area) before getting constructive. JPM and XOM are quietly strong—both within 2% of 52-week highs, above both moving averages, with healthy RSIs in the high-50s/low-60s and positive relative strength. PG is the weakest name here: -19.5% drawdown, -8.7% below its 200-day mean, and -9.7% 12-week relative underperformance—a clear avoid until it can reclaim its 200-day.

views.note: Strong momentum with +9.2% weekly surge, near highs, and +5.8% 4w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below 233 (roughly the 50-day area).
Sitting at its 52-week high with extraordinary +85.9% 26w return and dominant relative strength, though +48% above the 200-day is extended; a break below 305 would change my view.
Healthy uptrend near highs with +14.2% above 200-day, moderate RSI of 58.6, and +5.2% 4w relative strength; invalidated below 310.
Only -0.6% from 52-week high, above both moving averages with positive relative strength on all timeframes; would cut below 118 (200-day area).
RSI 27 is deeply oversold and may produce a bounce, but the -7.9% 4w relative weakness and -4.9% gap below the 50-day mean signal broken short-term trend; need a reclaim of ~272 to turn long.
Persistent downtrend: -19.5% drawdown, -8.7% below 200-day, -9.7% 12w relative underperformance—no reason to own until price reclaims 155.
Flat near both moving averages with -11.5% 12w relative underperformance and -11.6% drawdown; no trend to follow in either direction until it breaks above 500 or below 460.
Spectacular +57.8% 26w run has it +39.5% above the 200-day, which is parabolic; near highs but 4w relative strength is flat—I'd wait for a pullback toward 580 before adding.
Middling RSI of 49.7 and flat 4w relative strength suggest consolidation; above the 200-day but -10.7% from highs—need a break above 195 to get interested.
The -42.6% drawdown from highs is a massive structural break despite a recent 4w bounce; sitting right at the 200-day with negative 12w relative strength—too damaged to trust yet.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse Demands Caution
memos.body: I see the strongest durable earnings profiles in NVDA and GOOGL this cycle. NVDA posted $57.01B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a 56.0% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt—extraordinary operating leverage on a clean balance sheet. GOOGL delivered $102.35B in revenue (+15.9% YoY) at a 34.2% net margin with minimal leverage ($14.79B debt), while MSFT's 35.7% net margin and 18.4% revenue growth remain best-in-class among mega-cap software names. On the other side, UNH's net margin collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or reserve pressures that I cannot underwrite until I see a credible path back to mid-single-digit margins. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3%, and at an 8.8% net margin the earnings trajectory is clearly compressing.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, and only $8.47B debt make this the highest-quality earnings compounder in the universe; a sustained margin decline below 45% would change my view.
34.2% net margin on $102B revenue with 33% net income growth and low leverage ($14.79B debt) reflects durable, diversified earnings power.
35.7% net margin and 18.4% revenue growth on $77.67B quarterly revenue demonstrate consistent cloud-driven earnings expansion, though 12.5% net income growth lags revenue growth slightly.
Net margin expanded to 11.8% with 38.2% net income growth on $180B revenue, but I need to see margin durability above 10% for several more quarters given heavy capex commitments.
86.4% net income growth is impressive but partly reflects a prior-year comparison effect; 7.9% revenue growth is modest and $90.68B in total debt is the highest in the universe ex-JPM.
31% net margin and 11.6% net income growth are solid for a bank, but the $427B debt load and rate-cycle sensitivity limit my conviction on forward earnings durability.
Stable 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but only 3% revenue growth caps upside in a defensive name.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, compressing the margin to 13%; I need to see cost discipline restore earnings leverage before getting constructive.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% net margin on $113B revenue—this is severe cash-flow compression and I will not underwrite recovery until margins stabilize above 4%.
Revenue down 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin signals commodity-driven earnings erosion; a rebound in realized prices would change my view.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Benign Inflation and Stable Labor Market – Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Banks
memos.body: I see a clear mid-cycle easing regime: the Fed has cut 75 bp over the past year to a 3.75% upper bound, CPI is running at 2.7% y/y (close to target), and unemployment has drifted only modestly higher to 4.4% with no acceleration in the last three months. The 10y yield at 4.18% is down 50 bp y/y while the 2s10s curve has steepened to +70 bp, a positive signal for bank net interest margins and a tailwind for long-duration equities. I have conviction that further easing is likely unless CPI re-accelerates above 3% or unemployment spikes—either print would change my regime call. Cyclicals and energy lack a strong macro catalyst given the soft-but-stable growth backdrop, so I am more cautious there relative to growth and financials.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits directly from falling rates and a steepening curve in a benign inflation environment.
Lower rates support consumer spending power and equity multiples for high-quality duration assets; 2.7% CPI keeps real income growth positive.
Curve steepening (+31 bp y/y on 2s10s) directly boosts NIM while easing cycle supports credit quality with unemployment stable at 4.4%.
High-growth, long-duration name benefits from rate cuts, though elevated valuation means any inflation surprise would hit it hardest.
Consumer-facing cyclical growth supported by easing policy and stable employment; lower discount rates lift DCF valuations.
Defensive staples offer less upside in an easing/soft-landing regime where risk assets are favored; 2.7% CPI is manageable for margins but not a catalyst.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind—growth is soft but not recessionary, and easing policy doesn't directly boost commodity demand.
Classic cyclical that needs accelerating growth to outperform; flat unemployment and modest easing suggest a muddle-through rather than a capex boom.
Defensive healthcare is less rate-sensitive; macro backdrop neither helps nor hurts, so I have no strong directional view.
Ad-driven growth benefits from stable employment and consumer spending; falling rates support multiples for large-cap tech.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Universe; NVDA Post-Earnings Negativity Already Priced, XOM Reg-FD Filing Bears Watching
memos.body: I have very little GDELT-style media tone data to work with this cycle—the evidence set is dominated by routine 8-K filings (mostly director/officer changes) that generate minimal narrative shifts. The one concrete data point is NVDA's Q3 results 8-K on 2025-11-19, which triggered a -3.2% price reaction into the next close; that negative tone is now nearly two months old and likely fully absorbed. XOM stands out with three 8-K filings in quick succession, including a Reg-FD disclosure on 2026-01-07, which could signal a proactive narrative management effort ahead of earnings—worth monitoring for tone inflection. AAPL filed two director/officer 8-Ks in a month (Dec 5 and Jan 2), which is unusual cadence and could attract governance-focused media attention, though I have no tone data confirming that yet. Overall, I see no strong sentiment-driven trades here and assign low confidence across the board.

views.note: Post-earnings negative tone from Nov 19 (-3.2% reaction) is stale and likely priced after nearly two months.
Three 8-K filings in under two months including a fresh Reg-FD disclosure suggest active narrative management, but direction of tone is unclear.
Two director/officer 8-Ks in a month is elevated cadence that could draw governance scrutiny, but no media tone data confirms a shift.
Recent 8-K covering officer changes and bylaw amendments is routine; no sentiment signal detected.
Single officer departure 8-K from late November with no follow-up filings or tone data to act on.
Director/officer change filing in December is standard succession planning with no discernible media tone impact.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty Persists Despite Calm Credit Markets; Oil Weakness Signals Demand or Supply Shift Worth Monitoring
memos.body: I note a striking divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 474.73, up 34% over three months, while VIX has actually declined 5.2% over the same period and HY spreads have tightened 8bp. This tells me markets are pricing geopolitical and policy risk as noise rather than structural—a posture I find complacent given the magnitude of the uncertainty spike, which historically correlates with trade-policy or sanctions escalation. WTI crude at $57.74, down nearly 9% over three months, could reflect weakening global demand or an easing of supply constraints, either of which has differentiated implications across our universe. XOM's Jan 7 Reg FD filing suggests the company is actively managing investor communication amid this oil price environment. I have moderate conviction that semiconductor export-control risk and China-policy uncertainty remain the key structural geopolitical overhang for NVDA and AAPL, while energy-exposed names face a more cyclical headwind; a formal tightening of chip export rules or new tariff announcements would sharply change my views.

views.note: The 34% 3m surge in policy uncertainty likely reflects ongoing semiconductor export-control debates; any broadening of China chip restrictions would be a material negative, but current market pricing appears sanguine.
Supply-chain concentration in China and elevated policy uncertainty warrant caution, though tight credit spreads suggest no imminent macro stress; a tariff escalation would shift me to avoid.

WTI at $57.74 and falling 9% over three months pressures upstream margins; the Jan 7 Reg FD disclosure suggests management is proactively addressing investors, which often signals near-term earnings headwinds.

Lower oil prices reduce logistics costs, and benign credit conditions (HY OAS 2.76%) support consumer spending; policy uncertainty is less directly threatening to AMZN's diversified model than to hardware exporters.

A steepening yield curve (+15bp over 3m) hints at improving growth expectations that benefit cyclicals, but elevated policy uncertainty and weak oil (which dampens energy capex) create offsetting risks.
Steeper 10y-2y spread at 0.70pp and tight HY OAS support net interest margins and credit quality; geopolitical risk is manageable for a diversified bank absent a sanctions shock.
